each-ai-conversation-starts-fresh.header: Mollick's metaphor and the Claude Code example
each-ai-conversation-starts-fresh.description: Ethan Mollick offers the rule of thumb to treat AI "like an infinitely patient new coworker who forgets everything you tell them each new conversation" [1]. That is a metaphor, not a claim about every product. Anthropic documents that Claude Code sessions begin with a new conversation context; project instructions and files may still provide context [2].

anthropic-claude-code-memory.title: Anthropic, How Claude remembers your project

three-mornings.title: Three mornings
three-mornings.script: So the next morning you open a new conversation. In this example, the app supplies no history from yesterday. The pilot greets you with "Nice to meet you", you explain how to take the sediment sample, and the robot waits on deck while you talk. A real app may carry over chat history or saved memory; this story holds those features aside so we can see the problem of repeating a procedure.

the-hook.title: The hook
the-hook.script: That can happen when an app does not carry a procedure into a later request. You may have explained it many times, but the new context may not include those explanations. A saved skill is a separate file the app can provide; it does not change the model's training or memory.

what-would-you-do.title: What would you do
what-would-you-do.script: So here is my question, and I would like your honest answer: if you worked with this model for a whole season, what would you do about it? If you're with me in a workshop, type it into the chat now. If you're watching the recording, pause here and answer out loud. I'll come back to it.
